meta.rationale: G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storming is likely 01-02 Aug with the arrival of the 28 Jul CME event.

A slight chance for S1 (Minor) solar radiation storms will persist throughout the forecast period. This is  first due to any additional enhancement and excitement with the arrival of the 28 Jul CME, and then as AR 3380 continues to exhibit development as it rotates into a more favorable connection location.

R1-2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts from M-class flare activity is likely, along with a slight chance for an isolated R3 (Strong) radio blackout from an X-class flare, through the forecast period primarily due to Regions 3380 and 3386.
G1 (Minor) storming is likely during the early portions of 02 Aug with any lingering effects from the 28 Jul CME, although, confidence is low at this time.
A slight chance for a S1 (Minor) solar radiation storm will persist through 03 Aug until AR 3880 rotates beyond the southwestern limb.
R1-2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts remain likely through 03 Aug until AR 3880 rotates beyond the southwestern limb.
G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storming is likely to commence by late on 04 Aug and continue into 05 Aug due to CME events that left the sun over the course of 01 and 02 Aug.
A slight chance for an S1 (Minor) solar radiation event will persist through 03 Aug primarily due to the past activity and current potential presented by AR 3380 on the southwestern limb.

R1-2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely, with a slight chance for an isolated R3 (Strong) radio blackout, through 03 Aug primarily due to AR 3380. Probabilities decrease to just a chance by 04 Aug and remain so through 05 Aug as AR 3380 rotates off the visible solar disk.
G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storming is likely to commence by late on 04 Aug and continue into 05 Aug due to CME events that left the sun over the course of 01 and 02 Aug.
A slight chance for an S1 (Minor) solar radiation event will persist through 04 Aug primarily due to the past activity and current potential presented by AR 3380 on the southwestern limb.

R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely, with a slight chance for an isolated R3 (Strong) radio blackout, through 04 Aug. Probabilities decrease to just a chance by 05 Aug and remain so through 06 Aug.
G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storms are expected on 05 Aug due to CME influence from activity that occurred on the Sun over 01-02 Aug.
There is a slight chance for S1 (Minor) conditions on 05 Aug.
R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely on 05 Aug, with a chance for R1-R2 events on 06-07 Aug.
G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storms are likely on 08 Aug due to anticipated CME influence.

S1 (Minor) solar radiation storms are expected on 06 Aug. A further enhancement to the S2 (Moderate) levels is possible due to the X1.6 flare from Region 3386. There is a good chance for the proton event to continue on 07 Aug.
R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) are likely with a slight chance for R3 (Strong) over 06-07 Aug. Activity is expected to decrease to a chance for R1-R2 on 08 Aug with the departure of Region 3386.
G1 (Minor) geomagnetic storms are likely on 08 Aug due to anticipated CME influence.
There is a chance for S1 (Minor) solar radiation storms over 07-09 Aug.

R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely on 07 Aug due primarily to active regions on the Sun's western limb. A chance for R1-R2 exists over 08-09 Aug as the most active region rotates off of the visible disk.
G2 (Moderate) geomagnetic storms are likely to be reached in response to anticipated CME arrivals on 08 Aug.

S1 (Minor) solar radiation storms are expected on 08 Aug due to gradually increasing greater than 10 MeV proton flux levels. Additionally, any shock arrival from anticipated CMEs would likely increase the proton flux further.
R1-R2 (Minor-Moderate) radio blackouts are likely 08-09 Aug due in particular to the flare probability and activity trend of Region 3387.
